speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing. To help me understand your condition, have you noticed anything specific that triggers these episodes, or do they happen randomly?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The details you provided are concerning; the "muddy taste" and specific hand gestures suggest a focal onset, likely from the temporal lobe. To confirm if this is epilepsy, specifically temporal lobe epilepsy, I need to check his neurological status. REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram). Also, please describe exactly what those hand gestures looked like and if they involve a specific part of his body.
